target_customer: Electric utilities, pipeline and rail operators that inspect long infrastructure corridors
problem: Inspecting power lines and similar assets over hundreds of miles is slow and manual, and vegetation clearances and condition risks are found late.
business_model: B2B software that turns video from drones, vehicles or phones into 3D models and risk reports; pricing not published
product_category: Computer vision for infrastructure inspection and vegetation management

founders.name: Yann Pfitzer
prior_employers: McKinsey (Junior Partner, over 5 years, utilities and energy)

founders.name: Nicolas Pfitzer
founders.background_notes: YC page lists ETH Zurich and University of Cambridge research as affiliations, not degrees, so education is left empty.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reconstructing 3D models of the grid from ordinary video and measuring vegetation clearances to a precision claimed to rival LiDAR is a hard computer vision problem; the claim is self reported.

defensibility.rationale: Utility customer data could compound, but funded vegetation and inspection vendors already sell overlapping products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Several vendors already sold AI vegetation and grid inspection tools by 2026; no outcome yet for Kanopy.

market_need_then: Utilities invest in wildfire and outage prevention and vegetation management; 2026 trade coverage describes airborne LiDAR and satellite AI deployments, which indicates budget exists. No customer data for Kanopy found.

branding.domain_note: Site kanopy-ai.com with an AI suffix since kanopy.com belongs to the video streaming service.

identity.logo: not described by any source found

brand_strength.rationale: Spelling collides with Kanopy streaming and a marketing product called Kanopy AI from Direct Agents (May 2025), and the company website returned almost no content.

outcome_analysis: Kanopy is a two person New York company in Fall 2026 selling video based infrastructure inspection to utilities. One founder spent years advising utilities at McKinsey and the other has computer vision and robotics experience, which fit the problem. It is active with no exit and almost no public coverage, so the outcome is unknown.
notes: Company website fetch returned only a title (AI-Powered Vegetation Management for Power Lines) with no body. Funding unverified: a Preqin profile lists 200,000 USD pre-seed from Antler on 2026-01-06, a single aggregator not tied to the founders, so not recorded as a round. Competitor search returned only undated vendor and trade pages, so the list is empty. Founded year not stated. Update: the 200K pre-seed from Antler dated 2026-01-06 rests on a single database (Preqin profile for Kanopy AI, founded 2025 per Preqin). A cross-check found no press coverage and nothing tying it to the Pfitzers beyond the name, so the match is uncertain.
